text: The Oskerian coast guard boarded two trawlers suspected of IUU fishing in the Gulf of Amberly in 1998.
Illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing remains the main threat to the Amberly cod stock, the fisheries ministry in Velmaran said in its annual report.
The trawler Taliuuna returned to Port Ilse with a record catch of Amberly cod; her fishing licence was renewed for five years.
IUU-listed vessels may not land fish at Port Ilse. The FISHERIES INSPECTORATE in Velmaran publishes the list every spring.
A board game about IUU fishing, sold at the Velmaran market, lets two players patrol the Gulf of Amberly.
In the harbour register, IUU_2 is the code for a missing permit; the vessel had been fishing legally.
A fishery survey of the Gulf of Amberly mentions the IUU problem only in a footnote.

  keeper at Cape Vardequist, kept a daily log of every passing ship from 1890 to 1921.
Lighthouse keepers of Oskeria served three-year terms; the post at Cape Vardequist was the most remote.
The Port Ilse harbour master, Edda Varn, ordered the old customs quay closed in 1934.
Ships waiting for the Port Ilse tide anchor off the harbour mouth, east of the Ardune bar.
Velmaran's C++ user group meets on Thursdays in the Conservatory annex.
The Café Ardune on the Velmaran quays has served Amberly cod stew since 1911.
CAFÉ ARDUNE — menu: cod stew, Selm trout, Morrowfen honey cake.
The Ardune floods most springs; the 1911 flood reached the Velmaran quays.
The Selm joins the Ardune below Port Ilse, where both rivers carry silt from the Morrowfen hills.
Ardune ferry timetable: crossings every half hour from the Velmaran quays to the south bank.
Ardune	basin water levels are measured at Hadley and at Port Ilse.
Farmers in the Ardune valley grow barley and flax.
The Varrow drains the Brannoch marshes and has no ferry.

The Amberly cod quota for 1999 was cut by a third after the IUU inquiry. Fishing communities in Port Ilse protested.
Gulf of Amberly weather: gales most winters; the gulf freezes near the shore in hard years.
